Title: As a visitor I can register and log in so that I can access my account
Description: Email/password registration and login issuing a JWT in an HTTP-only cookie.
Acceptance Criteria: Password is hashed; invalid credentials are rejected without revealing which field was wrong; session persists across reload.

Title: As a user I can reset a forgotten password so that I am not locked out
Description: Emailed reset token with expiry.
Acceptance Criteria: Token is single-use and expires in 10 minutes; only a hash is stored; old sessions are invalidated after reset.

Title: As an organiser I can create an event with images so that it can be discovered
Description: Event creation with cover image upload to Cloudinary.
Acceptance Criteria: Required fields validated; cover image uploads and renders; slug generated; event appears in my events.

Title: As a visitor I can browse and open events so that I can decide what to attend
Description: Public listing with trending and upcoming plus event detail page.
Acceptance Criteria: Listing paginates; detail page shows date time location and ticket tiers; no auth required.

Title: As the team we have a layered backend architecture so that logic stays testable
Description: Controller to Service to Repository to Model separation.
Acceptance Criteria: No controller imports a repository; no service imports a Mongoose model; services take no req/res.

Title: As the team we have a repository and branching strategy so that work integrates safely
Description: Git workflow with dev and main plus pull requests.
Acceptance Criteria: Feature branches merge via PR; main stays releasable; commits link to work items.

Title: As a buyer I can purchase a ticket so that I can attend
Description: Checkout flow with buyer details and Paystack payment.
Acceptance Criteria: Multiple buyers supported in one checkout; guest checkout works without an account; confirmation screen shows the ticket.

Title: As the business inventory is reserved atomically so that we never oversell
Description: Guarded atomic increment inside a transaction.
Acceptance Criteria: Two concurrent purchases of the last seat result in exactly one success; proven by an integration test against a replica set.

Title: As the business payment is confirmed server-side so that a client cannot fake success
Description: Paystack webhook verified by HMAC-SHA512 over the raw body.
Acceptance Criteria: A forged or unsigned webhook changes no state; a tampered body is rejected; verification is unit-tested.

Title: As a buyer my seat is held before I pay so that I am never charged without a ticket
Description: Reserve then pay then confirm flow with a 15 minute hold.
Acceptance Criteria: Seats are held before checkout opens; abandoned holds are released; confirmation is idempotent under webhook retries.

Title: As a buyer I receive a QR ticket by email so that I can get in
Description: Ticket email containing an inline QR encoding the ticket ID.
Acceptance Criteria: Email sends only after payment is confirmed; QR encodes the scannable ticket ID; delivery failure does not void the booking.

Title: As door staff I can scan a QR so that I can admit a guest quickly
Description: Camera scanner using BarcodeDetector with manual code entry alongside.
Acceptance Criteria: Scans in under two seconds; manual entry always available; works on mobile.

Title: As the business a ticket admits exactly once so that it cannot be reused
Description: Atomic guarded check-in inside a transaction.
Acceptance Criteria: Two simultaneous scans of one ticket admit exactly once; the loser receives a clear rejection reason; proven by a concurrency test.

Title: As an organiser I can assign ushers so that only my staff can admit
Description: Usher assignment scoped to specific events.
Acceptance Criteria: An usher can only admit for assigned events; assignment and removal take effect immediately; rules are unit-tested.

Title: As an organiser every scan is logged so that entry is auditable
Description: Append-only audit log of every scan attempt.
Acceptance Criteria: Both admissions and rejections are recorded with actor outcome and reason; the log is never updated in place.

Title: As door staff I can admit manually so that a broken screen does not stop the queue
Description: Manual check-in fallback using the same authorisation rule as scanning.
Acceptance Criteria: An assigned usher can admit manually; the action is logged as manual; it is excluded from anomaly detection.

Title: As the team admission logic is unit-tested without a database so that rules stay verifiable
Description: Pure authorisation functions exported for testing.
Acceptance Criteria: Authorisation matrix covered for all four roles; tests run with no database or HTTP layer.

Title: As an organiser I can run an invite-only event so that entry is by guest list
Description: Access mode of public invite_only or hybrid on one event schema.
Acceptance Criteria: Purchase is refused for invite-only events; sales dates are not required for them; hybrid supports both paths.

Title: As an organiser I can import a guest list from CSV or Excel so that setup is fast
Description: Bulk guest import with parsing and validation.
Acceptance Criteria: Both CSV and xlsx parse; malformed rows are reported not silently dropped; re-importing does not duplicate guests.

Title: As a guest I receive a single-use QR invite so that I can be admitted
Description: Invite token issuance with emailed QR.
Acceptance Criteria: Token is cryptographically random and unique; the same scanner endpoint admits invite and purchased guests.

Title: As an organiser I see arrivals live so that I can manage the door
Description: Live dashboard over Server-Sent Events.
Acceptance Criteria: Admissions appear without refresh; only the event owner or an admin can subscribe; the initial snapshot is populated on connect.

Title: As an organiser I can add one guest at a time so that small changes are not painful
Description: Single-guest form alongside bulk import.
Acceptance Criteria: A guest can be added without a file; the invite issues immediately; validation matches the bulk path.

Title: As an organiser I can erase a guest's data on request so that we meet GDPR obligations
Description: Per-guest erasure plus a scheduled retention sweep.
Acceptance Criteria: Personal data is anonymised not deleted so counts survive; erasure is timestamped; the sweep is idempotent.

Title: As an organiser suspicious scan patterns are flagged so that fraud is visible
Description: Rule-based anomaly detection over the audit log.
Acceptance Criteria: Detects repeated rejects multi-device and rapid sequential patterns; evaluated with precision and recall against labelled fixtures.

Title: As an organiser I can ask questions in plain English so that I need no training
Description: Natural-language querying over the guest list.
Acceptance Criteria: Handles who has not arrived and how many VIPs checked in; intent parsing evaluated for accuracy; unknown intents fail gracefully.

Title: As an organiser I see expected no-shows so that I can plan capacity
Description: Logistic no-show model trained offline and scored at runtime.
Acceptance Criteria: Scores only pending bookings; surfaced on the dashboard; model evaluation report committed.

Title: As the team each model is evaluated with metrics so that claims are evidenced
Description: Evaluation harnesses for all three analytics features.
Acceptance Criteria: Each feature has a reproducible evaluation script or report; results are committed to the repository.

Title: As the business expired data is anonymised automatically so that retention is compliant
Description: Scheduled GDPR retention sweep.
Acceptance Criteria: Events past their retention window have attendee data anonymised; the sweep is safe to re-run; behaviour is integration-tested.

Title: As a user with a disability the interface meets WCAG 2.2 AA so that I can use it
Description: Accessibility audit and remediation against named success criteria.
Acceptance Criteria: Form labels present; status messages announced; contrast meets 4.5 to 1; focus is always visible.

Title: As the team CI runs tests on every change so that regressions are caught
Description: GitHub Actions pipeline for backend tests and frontend checks.
Acceptance Criteria: Backend suite runs against a real replica set; frontend typecheck lint and component tests run; a failure blocks the merge.

Title: As the team the stack runs from one command so that it is reproducible
Description: Docker Compose covering database API and frontend.
Acceptance Criteria: docker compose up builds and starts everything; the replica set initialises automatically; documented in the README.

Title: As door staff I am stopped at venue capacity so that we do not breach fire safety
Description: Occupancy enforcement at the door with an auditable supervisor override.
Acceptance Criteria: Admission is refused at capacity; the override is explicit per scan and recorded in the audit log; events with no capacity set are unaffected.

Title: As the team ticket IDs are server-issued so that a buyer cannot choose their own code
Description: Cryptographically random unique ticket identifiers generated server-side.
Acceptance Criteria: The client cannot supply a ticket ID; identifiers are unique by database index; a migration reconciles existing data.

Title: As the team usability is tested with real users so that design claims are evidenced
Description: ISO 9241-11 usability study with SUS.
Acceptance Criteria: Five participants across three scenarios; effectiveness efficiency and satisfaction measured; at least one defect fixed and re-tested.

Title: As the team component tests cover the frontend so that rendering logic is verified
Description: Vitest and React Testing Library setup with component tests.
Acceptance Criteria: Tests run headlessly in CI; the ticket QR and capacity override flows are covered.

Title: As an attendee I can meet other attendees so that events feel social
Description: Meet and Greet attendee directory with opt-in and live presence.
Acceptance Criteria: Only attendees holding a booking can see the directory; opting in is explicit and reversible; presence updates live over SSE.

Title: As an attendee I can chat with everyone at the event so that I can join the conversation
Description: Event Chat (Public) channel with server-sent live updates.
Acceptance Criteria: Messages persist and reload; posting requires the event to be live; the channel is scoped to one event.

Title: As an attendee I can message someone privately so that I can follow up one to one
Description: Direct messages between attendees of the same event.
Acceptance Criteria: A thread is visible only to its two participants; both must be eligible for that event.

Title: As a guest without an account I can join the Meet and Greet so that I am not excluded
Description: Email one-time-code access proving control of the booking address.
Acceptance Criteria: A six digit code is emailed and expires in ten minutes; only its hash is stored; the response does not reveal whether an address holds a ticket.

Title: As a visitor I can ask questions in plain English so that I can find the right event
Description: AI concierge chatbot backed by a language model with tool calling.
Acceptance Criteria: The bot searches events answers event questions and handles FAQs; it degrades to a fixed reply when no provider key is configured.

Title: As an attendee I am told what to wear and expect so that I arrive prepared
Description: Weather and dress code advice from Open-Meteo combined with organiser supplied event details.
Acceptance Criteria: Advice uses the real forecast within the sixteen day horizon and says so beyond it; it carries an explicit disclaimer that it is not a crime risk assessment.

Title: As an organiser I can describe my venue fully so that attendees know what to expect
Description: Extended event fields for venue dress code parking accessibility and age restriction.
Acceptance Criteria: New fields are optional and appear on the event page and in chatbot answers; existing events are unaffected.

Title: As the platform administrators cannot be self registered so that access cannot be escalated
Description: Signup role whitelist restricting self assignment to user and creator.
Acceptance Criteria: A crafted admin role in a signup request is discarded; the fix is verified against a running server.

Title: As the root administrator I control who becomes an administrator so that privilege is not shared freely
Description: Root admin bootstrap by CLI plus guarded role change.
Acceptance Criteria: Only the root admin may grant or revoke admin; nobody may change their own role or demote the root admin; decisions are unit tested.

Title: As an administrator I can remove events and users so that the platform can be moderated
Description: Soft delete of events and users preserving all referencing records.
Acceptance Criteria: Archived records disappear from every listing; bookings guests chat and audit rows survive; ushers are unassigned from archived events.

Title: As the team we know how much code is tested so that quality claims are evidenced
Description: Coverage measurement for both packages emitting lcov with no failing threshold.
Acceptance Criteria: Both packages produce an lcov report; CI archives it; no threshold blocks the build until a baseline is trusted.

Title: As the team we know the system holds under load so that performance is measured not assumed
Description: Load test harness against the hottest read endpoints.
Acceptance Criteria: Throughput is recorded for event list and detail; the rate limit is configurable so a run is not throttled to nothing.

Title: As the team the backend is linted in CI so that defects are caught before merge
Description: Blocking backend lint step added to the pipeline and CI extended to the dev branch.
Acceptance Criteria: Lint runs before the database is provisioned; CI triggers on both main and dev; a lint failure blocks the merge.
